To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a locus in a gene region on chromosome Xba I polymorphisms of the glycogen gene may serve as a thrifty gene that increases susceptibility for insulin resistance and hypertension when exposed to other factors, such as obesity or diabetes mellitus.
XbaI polymorphism of the GS gene is associated with insulin resistance in hypertension and that the A1 allele is a marker for insulin sensitivity in hypertension.

the A2 allele of glycogen synthase is enriched in hypertensive subjects with NIDDM in their family history and is associated with decreased glucose storage in skeletal muscles of hypertensive subjects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis of insulin resistance in hypertensive and NIDDM subjects.
the genetic basis of insulin resistance in hypertensive patients with a family history for NIDDM.
the genetic and environmental factors that influence the risk for developing hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Xba I polymorphic site in the glycogen synthesis gene may be associated with the development of hypertension and non-insulin dependent diabetes mellitus.
the Xba I polymorphisms of the GYS gene are associated with hypertension and NIDDM in a subgroup of subjects with a family predisposition for NIDDM.
the Xba I glycogen synthase polymorphism may be a genetic marker for the development of hypertension in subjects with NIDDM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a polymorphism of the gene for muscle glycogen synthetase is associated with hypertension and noninsulin-dependent diabetes mellitis (NIDDM).

the Xba I polymorphisms in the gene for glycogen synthase is associated with hypertension in nondiabetic subjects with a family hystory of NIDDM, and that the Xba A2 allele is associated with insulin resistance in hypertensive subjects.
the A2 allele of glycogen synthase is associated with insulin resistance and increased risk for NIDDM and hypertension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a genetic basis for insulin resistance.
the glycogen synthetase gene polymorphism (XbaI A2 allele) is associated with insulin resistance in hypertensive subjects with family history of NDIID.
the glycogen synthetase gene is a candidate gene for hypertension.
